```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Liu_2026_tislelizumab"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Liu_2026_tislelizumab"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.70649> (open access; supplementary
  Tables S1-S2 and Figure S1)
* Parent intravenous model: `modellib("Budha_2023_tislelizumab")`, Budha et
  al. (2023) <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12880>

Liu et al. extended the established intravenous population PK model of
tislelizumab, an anti-PD-1 IgG4 antibody, with two parallel first-order
subcutaneous absorption depots, one per injection site (abdomen and thigh;
Figure S1). Every disposition parameter, covariate effect, the disposition
IIV and the residual error were fixed to the intravenous-model estimates
(Table 1); only the absorption rate constant, the absolute bioavailability
and their IIV were estimated, separately per site. No covariate was retained
on the absorption parameters. The model was then used to simulate 300 mg SC
every 3 weeks (Q3W) against the approved 200 mg IV Q3W regimen and to select
thigh administration for phase 3.

# Population

The absorption model was fitted to 922 concentrations from 60 treatment-naive
adults with locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (ECOG
PS 0-1) in the phase 1 study BGB-A317-103 (NCT06091943; 15 sites in China and
Europe). In Part 1 (39 patients) each patient received 300 mg SC thigh,
300 mg SC abdomen and 200 mg IV in one of six randomized sequences over
Cycles 1-3 (Table S1), then 200 mg IV Q3W from Cycle 4; in Part 2 (21
patients) patients received 300 mg SC thigh Q3W throughout. Demographics are
reported in the primary clinical publication, not in this paper. The
disposition parameters come from the Budha 2023 pooled analysis (2596
patients, 12 studies; see the Budha 2023 article).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Liu_2026_tislelizumab")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source. "Fixed"
means the value was fixed to the intravenous-model estimate in Liu 2026.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lcl`, `lvc`, `lq`, `lvp`, `lq2`, `lvp2` | log(0.153 L/d), log(3.05 L), log(0.74 L/d), log(1.27 L), log(0.092 L/d), log(2.1 L); fixed | Liu 2026 Table 1 |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_alb_cl`, `e_tumsz_cl` | 0.565, -0.457, 0.0735; fixed | Liu 2026 Table 1 |
| `e_ada_cl`, `e_tumtp_gc_cl`, `e_tumtp_chl_cl` | 0.111, 0.069, -0.216; fixed | Liu 2026 Table 1 |
| `e_wt_vc`, `e_sexf_vc`, `e_age_vc` | 0.397, -0.116, 0.0966; fixed | Liu 2026 Table 1 |
| Covariate reference values | WT 65 kg, AGE 60 y, ALB 41 g/L, tumor size 63 mm | Budha 2023 Equations 5 and 6 (not restated in Liu 2026) |
| `lka_abdomen`, `lka_thigh` | log(0.247 1/d), log(0.189 1/d) | Liu 2026 Table 1 |
| `lfdepot_abdomen`, `lfdepot_thigh` | log(0.731), log(0.866) | Liu 2026 Table 1 |
| `etalcl`, `etalvc` variances | 0.263^2, 0.167^2; fixed | Liu 2026 Table 1 (omega on SD scale) |
| CL-Vc covariance | 0.020; fixed | Budha 2023 Table 3 (not printed in Liu 2026) |
| `etalvp`, `etalvp2` variances | 0.747^2, 0.999^2; fixed | Liu 2026 Table 1 |
| `etalka_abdomen`, `etalka_thigh` | 0.568^2, 0.382^2 | Liu 2026 Table 1 |
| `etalfdepot_abdomen`, `etalfdepot_thigh` | 0.264^2, 0.137^2 | Liu 2026 Table 1 |
| `propSd`, `addSd` | 0.126, 2.09 mg/L; fixed | Liu 2026 Table 1 |
| Two parallel SC depots into `central`, 3-compartment disposition | n/a | Liu 2026 Figure S1 |
| Covariate equations on CL and Vc | n/a | Budha 2023 Equations 5 and 6 |
| Combined additive + proportional residual error | n/a | Budha 2023 Equation 2 |

# Typical-patient profiles and a closed-form check

For the reference patient, a single dose over 21 days, and a long-horizon
check that the dose-normalised area ratio SC/IV recovers the absolute
bioavailability (`AUC0-inf = F * dose / CL` for linear kinetics).

```{r typical}
mod <- readModelDb("Liu_2026_tislelizumab")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

# zeroRe() removes the random effects on purpose; rxode2 warns on every
# multi-subject solve without omega, so muffle that one warning only.
solve_typical <- function(...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(...),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}

ref_cov <- data.frame(
  WT = 65, AGE = 60, ALB = 41, TUMSZ = 63, SEXF = 0, ADA_POS = 0,
  TUMTP_GASTRIC = 0, TUMTP_HODGKIN_CLASSICAL = 0
)
arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,                ~cmt,      ~amt, ~rate,
  "SC abdomen 300 mg", "depot",   300,  0,
  "SC thigh 300 mg",   "depot2",  300,  0,
  "IV 200 mg",         "central", 200,  200 / (1 / 24)
)

make_single <- function(i, tobs) {
  a <- arms[i, ]
  dose <- data.frame(
    id = i, time = 0, evid = 1, amt = a$amt, rate = a$rate, cmt = a$cmt
  )
  obs <- data.frame(
    id = i, time = tobs, evid = 0, amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = "central"
  )
  cbind(rbind(dose, obs), ref_cov, arm = a$arm)
}
tobs_short <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 21, by = 0.1), 1 / 24)))
ev_typ <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), make_single, tobs = tobs_short))
sim_typ <- solve_typical(mod_typ, events = ev_typ, keep = "arm") |>
  as.data.frame()

ggplot(sim_typ, aes(time, Cc, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (day)", y = "Tislelizumab (mg/L)", colour = NULL,
    title = "Typical reference patient, single dose"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r closed-form}
tobs_long <- c(seq(0, 2, by = 1 / 96), seq(2.05, 3000, by = 0.05))
ev_long <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), make_single, tobs = tobs_long))
sim_long <- solve_typical(
  mod_typ, events = ev_long, keep = "arm", atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10
) |>
  as.data.frame()

auc_long <- sim_long |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  arrange(time, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  summarise(
    auc = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2),
    c_last = last(Cc),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(arms |> select(arm, amt), by = "arm") |>
  mutate(
    expected = c(
      "SC abdomen 300 mg" = 0.731, "SC thigh 300 mg" = 0.866, "IV 200 mg" = 1
    )[arm] * amt / 0.153,
    pct_diff = 100 * (auc - expected) / expected
  )

auc_long |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Arm = arm, `AUC0-3000 d (mg*d/L)` = auc, `F * dose / CL` = expected,
    `% diff` = pct_diff
  ) |>
  select(-c_last, -amt) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

# The solve and the closed form share the same parameters, so the only
# difference is trapezoidal and truncation error.
stopifnot(all(abs(auc_long$pct_diff) < 0.5), all(auc_long$c_last < 1e-3))
```

# Virtual cohort

The phase 3 dose-selection simulations assumed first-line gastric-cancer
patients (BGB-A317-305; Table S2): albumin, body weight, age and baseline
tumor burden normally distributed and simulated independently, sex and
treatment-emergent ADA status sampled from the four sex-by-ADA categories.
The normals are truncated to the Table S2 ranges. The paper simulated 1000
trials of 100 patients per arm; one cohort of 200 patients per arm is used
here, with the same 200 covariate sets in each arm.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(70649)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(70649)
n_per_arm <- 200

rtnorm <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) {
  x <- rnorm(n, mean, sd)
  bad <- x < lo | x > hi
  while (any(bad)) {
    x[bad] <- rnorm(sum(bad), mean, sd)
    bad <- x < lo | x > hi
  }
  x
}

sex_ada <- sample(1:4, n_per_arm, replace = TRUE)
covs <- data.frame(
  pid = seq_len(n_per_arm),
  ALB = rtnorm(n_per_arm, 40.02, 4.39, 26, 53),
  WT = rtnorm(n_per_arm, 60.83, 12.99, 32.1, 112.0),
  AGE = rtnorm(n_per_arm, 58.77, 11.09, 23, 86),
  TUMSZ = rtnorm(n_per_arm, 60.52, 48.95, 10, 384),
  SEXF = as.integer(sex_ada %in% c(3, 4)),
  ADA_POS = as.integer(sex_ada %in% c(2, 4)),
  TUMTP_GASTRIC = 1L,
  TUMTP_HODGKIN_CLASSICAL = 0L
)

dose_times <- seq(0, 84, by = 21)
tobs <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 105, by = 0.25), dose_times + 1 / 24)))

make_arm <- function(i) {
  a <- arms[i, ]
  ids <- (i - 1L) * n_per_arm + covs$pid
  dose <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = dose_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 1, amt = a$amt, rate = a$rate, cmt = a$cmt)
  obs <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = tobs) |>
    mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    mutate(pid = id - (i - 1L) * n_per_arm, arm = a$arm) |>
    left_join(covs, by = "pid") |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), make_arm))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")]))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, events = events, keep = "arm",
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, arm, fdepot_thigh, fdepot_abdomen)
sim$arm <- factor(sim$arm, levels = arms$arm)
```

The exponential IIV on bioavailability is not bounded at one, so some
simulated patients absorb more than the dose:

```{r f-above-one}
sim |>
  distinct(id, arm, fdepot_thigh, fdepot_abdomen) |>
  filter(arm != "IV 200 mg") |>
  mutate(f_i = ifelse(arm == "SC thigh 300 mg", fdepot_thigh, fdepot_abdomen)) |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(
    `median F` = median(f_i), `% of patients with F > 1` = 100 * mean(f_i > 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

# Replicate published figures

```{r figure-4, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
# Replicates Figure 4 of Liu 2026: Cycle 1 and steady-state (Cycle 5)
# profiles of 300 mg SC Q3W (thigh, abdomen) overlaid on 200 mg IV Q3W.
fig4 <- sim |>
  mutate(
    cycle = case_when(
      time <= 21 ~ "Cycle 1",
      time >= 84 ~ "Cycle 5 (steady state)",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    tcyc = ifelse(time >= 84, time - 84, time)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(cycle)) |>
  group_by(arm, cycle, tcyc) |>
  summarise(
    q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), q50 = median(Cc),
    q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(fig4, aes(tcyc, q50, colour = arm, fill = arm)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~cycle) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose in the cycle (day)", y = "Tislelizumab (mg/L)",
    colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates Figure 4 of Liu 2026. Lines: median; bands: 5th-95th",
      "percentiles of individual predictions (the paper's bands are",
      "percentiles of trial geometric means, so they are narrower)."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# PKNCA validation

Table 2 of the paper reports, per arm, the geometric mean (GM) of Cycle 1
Ctrough (Cycle 2 predose, day 21), Cycle 1 AUC0-21, steady-state Ctrough
(Cycle 5 predose, day 84) and Cycle 5 AUC0-21 (days 84-105). Each cycle is
re-anchored to start at time 0 for PKNCA. Cycle 1 Ctrough is the
end-of-interval `ctrough`; the steady-state Ctrough is `cmin` of Cycle 5,
which is its predose value because concentrations are still accumulating
(the Cycle 5 predose sample is the lowest of the cycle in every arm).

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(
    cycle = case_when(
      time <= 21 ~ "Cycle 1",
      time >= 84 ~ "Cycle 5",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    tcyc = round(ifelse(time >= 84, time - 84, time), 6)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(cycle)) |>
  select(id, arm, cycle, tcyc, Cc)

dose_nca <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1, time %in% c(0, 84)) |>
  mutate(
    cycle = ifelse(time == 0, "Cycle 1", "Cycle 5"),
    tcyc = 0
  ) |>
  select(id, arm, cycle, tcyc, amt)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ tcyc | arm + cycle + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca, amt ~ tcyc | arm + cycle + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = 21,
  cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, ctrough = TRUE, cmin = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_ind <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(
    PPTESTCD == "auclast" |
      (PPTESTCD == "ctrough" & cycle == "Cycle 1") |
      (PPTESTCD == "cmin" & cycle == "Cycle 5")
  ) |>
  mutate(PPTESTCD = ifelse(PPTESTCD == "cmin", "ctrough", PPTESTCD))
stopifnot(!anyNA(nca_ind$PPORRES), all(nca_ind$PPORRES > 0))

sim_gm <- nca_ind |>
  group_by(arm, cycle, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(PPORRES = exp(mean(log(PPORRES))), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(arm = as.character(arm))
```

## Comparison against published exposure metrics

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,                ~cycle,    ~ctrough, ~auclast,
  "SC abdomen 300 mg", "Cycle 1", 19.28,    532.24,
  "SC thigh 300 mg",   "Cycle 1", 23.86,    603.23,
  "IV 200 mg",         "Cycle 1", 14.52,    587.58,
  "SC abdomen 300 mg", "Cycle 5", 42.72,    1226.81,
  "SC thigh 300 mg",   "Cycle 5", 52.52,    1451.90,
  "IV 200 mg",         "Cycle 5", 33.08,    1135.77
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_gm,
  reference = published,
  by = c("arm", "cycle"),
  params = c("ctrough", "auclast"),
  units = c(ctrough = "mg/L", auclast = "mg*d/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = paste(
    "Geometric means, simulated (one cohort of 200 per arm) vs Liu 2026",
    "Table 2 (median of 1000 simulated trials). AUClast is AUC0-21 of the",
    "cycle. * differs from reference by more than 20%."
  )
)
```

The geometric-mean ratios SC/IV, which drove the dose selection:

```{r gmr}
gmr_pub <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,                ~cycle,    ~PPTESTCD,  ~published,
  "SC abdomen 300 mg", "Cycle 1", "ctrough",  1.33,
  "SC thigh 300 mg",   "Cycle 1", "ctrough",  1.64,
  "SC abdomen 300 mg", "Cycle 1", "auclast",  0.91,
  "SC thigh 300 mg",   "Cycle 1", "auclast",  1.03,
  "SC abdomen 300 mg", "Cycle 5", "ctrough",  1.29,
  "SC thigh 300 mg",   "Cycle 5", "ctrough",  1.59,
  "SC abdomen 300 mg", "Cycle 5", "auclast",  1.08,
  "SC thigh 300 mg",   "Cycle 5", "auclast",  1.28
)
gmr <- sim_gm |>
  filter(arm != "IV 200 mg") |>
  left_join(
    sim_gm |> filter(arm == "IV 200 mg") |> select(cycle, PPTESTCD, iv = PPORRES),
    by = c("cycle", "PPTESTCD")
  ) |>
  mutate(simulated = PPORRES / iv) |>
  select(arm, cycle, PPTESTCD, simulated) |>
  left_join(gmr_pub, by = c("arm", "cycle", "PPTESTCD"))

gmr |>
  mutate(PPTESTCD = ifelse(PPTESTCD == "ctrough", "Ctrough", "AUC0-21")) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Arm = arm, Cycle = cycle, Metric = PPTESTCD,
    `Simulated GMR` = simulated, `Published GMR` = published
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

pct_gm <- sim_gm |>
  inner_join(
    published |> pivot_longer(c(ctrough, auclast), names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "ref"),
    by = c("arm", "cycle", "PPTESTCD")
  ) |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * (PPORRES - ref) / ref)
stopifnot(
  # A mis-transcribed CL, F, ka or dose moves a geometric mean of 200
  # patients by tens of percent; Monte Carlo noise is a few percent.
  abs(median(pct_gm$pct)) < 10,
  all(abs(pct_gm$pct) < 20),
  all(abs(gmr$simulated - gmr$published) < 0.15)
)
```

Cycle 1 agrees with Table 2 within about 5% in every arm, and the SC/IV
ratios agree within about 0.1. The Cycle 5 geometric means run 6-14% below
Table 2 in all three arms alike, IV included, so the shortfall lies in
accumulation under the fixed disposition model, not in the estimated
absorption parameters. It is not explained by the trough timing: the Cycle 6
predose (day 105) trough and the days 105-126 AUC of this model are still
below the Table 2 values. Nor is it explained by the IIV scale: the Budha
2023 reading of the disposition variances moves these geometric means by
less than 4%. The remaining candidates are inputs the paper does not report,
such as the proportions of the four sex-by-ADA categories (ADA-positive
status raises CL by 12%) and the parameter-uncertainty draws.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **IIV scale.** Table 1 of Liu 2026 gives omega "on SD scale" in percent, so
  each variance is (value / 100)^2. The same percentages appear unlabelled in
  Budha 2023 Table 3, from which `modellib("Budha_2023_tislelizumab")`
  derived its variances as log(CV^2 + 1); the two readings agree within 4%
  for CL and Vc but differ for V3 (0.998 here, 0.692 there). This model follows
  the explicit Liu 2026 label.
- **CL-Vc covariance.** Liu 2026 fixed the disposition IIV to the intravenous
  model but does not print the CL-Vc covariance; the Budha 2023 Table 3
  value 0.020 (log scale) is used.
- **Covariate reference values** (65 kg, 60 years, 41 g/L, 63 mm) are not
  restated in Liu 2026; they are the Budha 2023 Equation 5 and 6 values the
  fixed effects were estimated with. "Baseline tumor burden" in Liu 2026 is
  the Budha 2023 tumor-size covariate (`TUMSZ`).
- **Bioavailability IIV** is exponential, the form Budha 2023 Equation 1 uses
  for every parameter, and the only form under which a percent omega on F is
  meaningful. Liu 2026 does not say whether individual F was capped at one; no
  cap is applied, so the model expects about 15% of thigh and 12% of abdomen
  injections to have F > 1 (the table above shows the realised fraction in
  this cohort).
- **Injection-site depots.** Figure S1 draws the abdomen and thigh depots as
  separate compartments (Depot 1 and Depot 2), so a patient who switches
  sites between cycles (Table S1) carries both depots at once. They are the
  parallel depots `depot` (abdomen) and `depot2` (thigh); dose the record into
  the compartment of the injection site.
- **Virtual population.** Sex-by-ADA categories are sampled with equal
  probability (the paper does not give the proportions), and the Table S2
  normals are truncated to the Table S2 ranges. The paper's simulations also
  included parameter uncertainty, which is not reproduced; it widens the
  spread of trial geometric means but leaves their median essentially
  unchanged.
- **Comparison metric.** Table 2 reports the median of 1000 trial geometric
  means (n = 100 per arm); the comparison above uses the geometric mean of
  one cohort of 200 per arm, computed from individual predictions without
  residual error.
- **Specimen.** The paper uses "plasma" and "serum" interchangeably; the
  compartments record serum, the matrix of the Table 2 trough endpoint.
- No erratum or correction notice for Liu 2026 was found as of 2026-11-13.
